text: sketchpad lightweight, p5.js-inspired drawing system generative art, built S7 classes grid graphics. bypasses ggplot2 entirely: small set drawable shapes (circle, blob, ribbon, twist, bezier) expose computed points property, composed sketch, rendered draw(). shared foundation extracted author’s personal generative-art sketchbook (sketches repo) intended depended various series-* generative art project repos.

title: AGENTS.md
text: style – container color/fill/linewidth, forwarded grid::gpar(). points – polygon’s vertices (x/y numeric vectors, equal length). drawable – parent class every shape. Declares two properties: style (default style()) computed points property subclasses override. meant instantiated directly. shape – trivial drawable: x/y supplied directly points. Usually produced convert(), constructed hand. circle – centroid + radius + n (point count); points n evenly-spaced points around circumference. blob – like circle, radius perturbed simplex noise (ambient::fracture()/ambient::gen_simplex()/ambient::fbm()), giving irregular outline. range controls noise amplitude, frequency/octaves/seed control noise field. ribbon – tapered band (x, y) (xend, yend), width modulated simplex noise sqrt taper goes zero ends. twist – like ribbon, underlying path smoothed Brownian bridge (e1071::rbridge() via internal smooth_bridge() helper) rather straight line. bezier – outline follows Bezier curve arbitrary number control points (x/y), evaluated via Bernstein polynomial basis (internal bernstein() helper, De Casteljau’s algorithm). Ported series-lissajous, redesigned: original bare S7_object producing curve data frame, consumed internally separate bezier_ribbon drawable. bezier parent = drawable, ’s directly usable draw() – cost always rendering closed polygon (curve’s last point connects straight back first), since every drawable’s points drawn grid::polygonGrob(). open/stroked-curve option. bezier_ribbon ported; see PLAN.md. sketch – list drawables (shapes property). Built sketch() + circle() + blob(...); + method requires S7 method registration, S3 `+.sketch` (see “Gotchas”). draw() – S7 generic, dispatch_args = "object". Methods drawable (single shape) sketch (renders every shape one shared, equal-aspect viewport); catch-method class_any warns returns invisible(NULL) anything else. xlim/ylim default range object’s points. convert() – S7’s generic (defined package); method(convert, list(drawable, shape)) “freezes” drawable’s computed points plain shape, preserving style.

title: AGENTS.md
text: Every drawable drawn single grid::polygonGrob() inside grid::viewport() equal-axis scaling (width/height set via "snpc" units 1:1 aspect ratio preserved regardless device’s aspect ratio). draw(sketch) computes one shared viewport/axis-range across every shape’s points, draws shape’s polygon list order – later shapes drawn top.

title: AGENTS.md
text: handful non-obvious S7 behaviors bite future edit forgotten – discovered manifest classes move sourced script installed package (see HISTORY.md full debugging narrative): S7 classes get namespace-qualified class names inside package ("sketchpad::sketch", "sketch"). check written inherits(x, "drawable") S3 method named `+.sketch` silently stops matching. Use S7::S7_inherits(x, drawable) inheritance checks, register operator methods S7 way: method(\+`, list(sketch, drawable)) <- function(e1, e2) {…}`. S7::methods_register() must called .onLoad() (R/sketchpad-package.R) whenever package defines method external/base generic (, +). Without , methods dispatch fine devtools::load_all() silently fail dispatch package actually installed – surfaced devtools::check(), interactive development. drawable’s shape(x = ..., y = ..., style = @style) shortcut doesn’t work. shape()’s constructor named x/y parameters; everything else ... forwarded style(...), passing style = <style object> tries call style(style = <...>) errors. convert() instead builds shape x/y alone, reassigns @style afterward. R sources R/*.R alphabetically default, breaks subclass definitions. blob.R needs drawable (drawable.R) exist first, “blob.R” < “drawable.R” alphabetically. Fixed explicit Collate field DESCRIPTION (see “Structure” required order) rather @include tags. first devtools::document() pass adding new cross-referencing class emits “resolve link” warnings. expected roxygen2 behavior several classes’ [link] references point none .Rd files exist yet; second document() call resolves . Don’t chase warning rewording docs. @export individual method(generic, class) <- function(...) assignment generates .Rd page \usage section won’t match hand-written @param docs (e.g. method’s xlim/ ylim formals aren’t part generic’s signature). Add #' @noRd alongside #' @export every method block; keep real documentation generic/class definition. R CMD check reports spurious “visible binding global variable properties” NOTE tied S7’s method<- internals misattributing symbol package’s code. Silenced utils::globalVariables("properties") R/sketchpad-package.R; known S7 artifact, real problem package’s code. sketch available package name. ’s existing CRAN package (R--JavaScript/p5.js transpiler) – installing collide. Named package sketchpad instead.

title: AGENTS.md
text: R/style.R, R/points.R, R/drawable.R – foundation classes, load order (depends previous). R/bezier.R, R/shape.R, R/circle.R, R/blob.R, R/ribbon.R, R/twist.R – concrete drawable subclasses, one file . R/sketch.R – sketch class + method. R/draw.R – draw generic three methods. R/convert.R – convert(drawable, shape) method. R/sketchpad-package.R – package-level doc, #' @import S7, .onLoad() calling S7::methods_register(), globalVariables("properties") workaround. DESCRIPTION’s Collate field pins load order explicitly (style -> points -> drawable -> bezier -> shape -> circle -> blob -> ribbon -> twist -> sketch -> draw -> convert -> sketchpad-package). new drawable subclass must added Collate drawable.R, devtools::load_all()/R CMD check fail “object ‘drawable’ found” error.

title: AGENTS.md
text: Fully qualify every call another package (S7::new_class(), grid::polygonGrob(), ambient::fracture(), …) inside R/*.R; bare (unqualified) symbols package’s exports plus whatever #' @import S7/#' @importFrom brings . library() calls anywhere R/. Use base R pipe (|>), magrittr pipe. Every concrete drawable follows constructor shape: constructor = function(<args>, ...) S7::new_object(drawable(), <args>, style = style(...)), arbitrary style arguments (color, fill, linewidth) always accepted via ... without subclass needing declare . computed geometry property (points, bezier/path twist) new_property() getter – geometry always derived, never stored mutated place. Every scalar numeric/integer constructor argument gets explicit length(x) != 1 check validator; every non-negative-argument (radius, width, range, frequency) gets < 0 check; every positive-integer argument (n, octaves) gets < 1L check. Keep new drawables consistent .

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: blob() circle whose radius perturbed simplex noise. six blobs arranged around ring, one per colour:
code: library(sketchpad) #>  #> Attaching package: 'sketchpad' #> The following object is masked from 'package:graphics': #>  #>     points  values <- tibble::tibble(   x = cos(seq(0, pi * 5 / 3, length.out = 6)),   y = sin(seq(0, pi * 5 / 3, length.out = 6)),   n = 500L,   fill = c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088"),   color = fill ) blobs <- purrr::pmap(values, blob) blobs |> sketch() |> draw()

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: Randomising position, radius, noise range many blobs gives organic composition:
code: set.seed(3) palette <- c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088") n_blobs <- 200L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_blobs, sd = 1.5),   y = rnorm(n_blobs, sd = 1.5),   n = 500L,   fill = sample(palette, n_blobs, replace = TRUE),   radius = runif(n_blobs),   range = runif(n_blobs, min = 0, max = .5),   color = fill ) blobs <- purrr::pmap(values, blob) blobs |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: ribbon() tapered, noise-displaced band drawn two points:
code: set.seed(3) palette <- c("#e50000", "#ff8d00", "#ffee00", "#028121", "#004cff", "#770088") n_ribbons <- 200L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_ribbons, sd = 1.5),   y = rnorm(n_ribbons, sd = 1.5),   xend = x + 1,   yend = y,   width = 1,   n = 500L,   fill = sample(palette, n_ribbons, replace = TRUE),   color = fill ) ribbons <- purrr::pmap(values, ribbon) ribbons |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: A Minimal Drawing System For Generative Art
text: twist() like ribbon, follows Brownian bridge instead straight line, giving wandering, twisted appearance:
code: set.seed(1) palette <- c("#de9151", "#f34213", "#2e2e3a", "#bc5d2e", "#bbb8b2") n_twists <- 400L values <- tibble::tibble(   x = rnorm(n_twists, sd = 2),   y = rnorm(n_twists, sd = 2),   xend = x + 1,   yend = y + rnorm(n_twists, sd = 1),   width = runif(n_twists, min = .1, max = .3),   smooth = 6L,   n = 100L,   fill = sample(palette, n_twists, replace = TRUE),   color = fill ) twists <- purrr::pmap(values, twist) twists |> sketch() |> draw(xlim = c(-2, 2), ylim = c(-2, 2))

title: A Bezier curve — bezier
text: bezier drawable whose outline follows Bezier curve defined arbitrary number control points (x, y). two control points straight line; four, cubic Bezier kind used build ribbons flowing shapes. Since draw() always renders drawable's points closed polygon, curve implicitly closed last control point back first.
